title: Borealis Finance - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
summary: Discovery call to understand Borealis Finance's inference needs. They run latency-sensitive customer-facing ML services and are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU pools with strict data isolation and burst capacity for peak trading windows. Main concerns: predictable throughput, multi-tenant isolation (VPC & network controls), SLA/uptime, support for rolling upgrades, and integration with their KMS and SSO. Next steps: share dedicated pricing/config sheet, security pack (SOC2/ISO docs), and schedule a technical deep-dive to scope benchmark tests on their representative workload.
next_steps: Jordan to share Dedicated pricing and config sheet by 2026-03-09
Anita to send security pack (SOC2 + ISO attestation + audit log sample) by 2026-03-06
Schedule technical deep dive / benchmark with Ethan and Maya for week of 2026-03-16
action_items: Jordan Reyes: send Dedicated pricing + sizing worksheet by 2026-03-09
Anita Kapoor: share security docs (SOC2/ISO/KMS integration notes) by 2026-03-06
Ethan Brooks: provide sample QPS and 99th pct latency targets + a small dataset for benchmark by 2026-03-11
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. Anita our SE is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya Patel: Good, thanks. We wanted to talk through Dedicated capacity details, isolation, bursts, all that.
[00:12] Anita Kapoor: Great, thanks Maya. Could you start with a quick overview of the product surface and the workloads you're targeting?
[00:20] Tom Hwang: Sure, quick context — Borealis runs a customer-facing recommendation and fraud signal scoring service. Latency critical, 50-200ms p95 is a must for some endpoints. We also do batch scoring but real-time is primary.
[00:35] Jordan Reyes: Understood. Are you currently using in-house GPUs or a managed API?
[00:40] Ethan Brooks: Mixed — internal infra for models that touch PII, and we use a couple of vendor APIs for other models. We're evaluating dedicated because we need reserved capacity plus stronger isolation and predictable costs.
[00:52] Anita Kapoor: When you say isolation, do you mean network-level VPC isolation, physical tenancy, and data residency?
[00:58] Sofia Martinez: All of the above. Our security and compliance team wants VPC peering or customer VPC option, CMKs for key management, full audit logs, and SOC2 evidence. Also can't have multi-tenant GPUs where other customers' workloads could be scheduled on the same underlying host.
[01:15] Anita Kapoor: Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed VPC peering and private deployments. For Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools — they're logically isolated and we support single-tenant nodes for customers with that requirement. For KMS we can integrate with your CMK via our Private offering and for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys in many regions.
[01:34] Maya Patel: What's the typical burst strategy? Our traffic pattern is spiky around market open/close windows. We need both guaranteed baseline throughput and a way to handle 2-3x spikes for 10-20 minutes.
[01:45] Jordan Reyes: We do reserved baseline capacity with burstable headroom. There's a configured burst pool and optional cloud burst to a compatible model variant on hosted fleet if needed, with policy controls. Question: how strict are the time windows and can you give us numbers?
[01:59] Tom Hwang: Market open is 09:30 to 09:45 and close 15:50 to 16:05 local — spikes up to 2.5x baseline QPS for ~12 minutes. Our baseline p95 latency target is 150ms, ideally 100ms for priority traffic.
[02:16] Anita Kapoor: Good, that's useful. For that pattern we'd size baseline reserved GPUs to meet steady QPS and configure burst policies for short spikes. Also recommend prefix/KV caching to shave token compute for long-context models.
[02:30] Ethan Brooks: How quickly does autoscaling act? We can't afford long warm-up times, GPUs take time to spin up.
[02:36] Anita Kapoor: Correct — GPU cold start is nontrivial. Our Dedicated autoscaler prefers warm pools and prewarmed instances; we have cold-start mitigations (warm pools, fast serialization, and model variants). For short 10-20 minute bursts we recommend maintaining a small warm buffer and using burst pools with lower-cost quantized variants as overflow.
[02:55] Maya Patel: What's the expected cost delta if we keep a warm buffer say 10% of baseline?
[03:01] Jordan Reyes: It depends on GPU type and utilization; typical guidance is 8-12% uplift vs pure reserved baseline. We'll include sample numbers in the pricing sheet.
[03:09] Sofia Martinez: On compliance: do you provide audit logs for all inference requests and admin actions? We need immutable logs for at least 1 year.
[03:18] Anita Kapoor: Yes, Dedicated includes audit logging with configurable retention; for longer retention we offer a log export pipeline to your S3 with object lock. SOC2 report and ISO certifications are available, we'll send that pack.
[03:31] Ethan Brooks: How about rolling upgrades and maintenance windows — we need predictable windows and can not have model evictions during peak hours.
[03:39] Anita Kapoor: We support configurable maintenance windows and can schedule non-disruptive rolling upgrades — the runtime supports live model handover and KV cache transfer but depends on your SLA tier. For strict anti-eviction guarantees we can provision single-tenant hosts.
[03:54] Tom Hwang: Networking: we need outbound egress restrictions and control plane traffic to be tunneled over our private link. Can you support that?
[04:02] Jordan Reyes: Yes, dedicated supports PrivateLink/VPC peering and control plane traffic over customer-managed tunnels for our Private offering; for Dedicated we can support VPC peering and firewall rules. We'll capture exact networking requirements in the tech dive.
[04:17] Maya Patel: A couple of technical questions — do you have deterministic 99th pct latency SLAs and how do you measure them? Also how are tokens billed for batch vs real-time?
[04:29] Anita Kapoor: We publish performance SLOs per model profile and measure p95/p99 at the token and request levels across routes; billing is per token for generation and per embedding unit for embeddings — for Dedicated you can choose fixed consumption buckets or metered usage. We'll outline options in the proposal.
[04:46] Ethan Brooks: For benchmarks, what's the recommended test harness? We want to run our prompt sets and a replay of live traffic to validate p95/p99 and cost projections.
[04:55] Anita Kapoor: We have a benchmarking harness and can run replay tests on a customer's sample traffic in a staging Dedicated pool — we typically ask for a representative dataset, QPS profiles, and acceptance criteria. We'll run three runs (cold, warm, steady) and provide latency and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:10] Tom Hwang: Any limitations on model types or quantization? We run custom fine-tuned models and some open models.
[05:16] Anita Kapoor: Dedicated supports custom model artifacts; we recommend quantization profiles for cost; some kernels behave differently at extreme sequence lengths. We'll need to review model size and sequence distribution.
[05:27] Maya Patel: Security integration — SSO, RBAC mapping to our Okta groups?
[05:31] Jordan Reyes: We support SAML/Okta, SCIM provisioning for RBAC groups, and granular route-level permissions. Anita can follow up with the mapping template.
[05:40] Sofia Martinez: Do you support HSM-backed keys? We need FIPS 140-2 for key storage.
[05:44] Anita Kapoor: For Private we support HSM/KMS integrations. For Dedicated we integrate with cloud KMS and can support customer-managed keys; HSM-backed workflows are available in the Private/on-prem option — we'll include specifics.
[05:58] Maya Patel: Timeline and procurement — if we like the benchmark, what's typical lead time to stand up Dedicated capacity?
[06:04] Jordan Reyes: Baseline: 4-6 weeks for provisioning and networking (assuming approvals), faster for standard configs; single-tenant or private deployments add 2-4 weeks.
[06:13] Tom Hwang: Budget — we have an annual commit process; want to understand committed vs metered options.
[06:19] Jordan Reyes: We offer reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated with monthly/annual commits and pricing tiers based on GPU class and utilization; we'll include commit examples and estimated TCO in the pricing doc.
[06:30] Ethan Brooks: On-call and SLA — do you provide 24/7 NOC and a named CSM?
[06:34] Jordan Reyes: Yes for enterprise tiers we provide a named CSM and 24/7 support with escalation paths. SLA credits available for uptime misses.
[06:42] Maya Patel: Anything we should be aware of regarding data residency/region availability for our EU customers?
[06:47] Anita Kapoor: We have regions in NA and EU; for Private deployments we can support on-prem or customer region-only options for strict residency.
[06:56] Tom Hwang: If we proceed, what does the pilot look like? We'd want a pilot with 2-4 reserved GPUs sized to high-priority workloads and a replay benchmark.
[07:05] Anita Kapoor: That's reasonable. Pilot typically 2-6 weeks with benchmarks and then scale plan for production.
[07:10] Jordan Reyes: Ok, let's recap next steps. I'll share pricing and sizing, Anita will send security docs and benchmark plan, Ethan to provide traffic/sample dataset. Any other items?
[07:21] Sofia Martinez: Please include contact for compliance questions and sample audit logs.
[07:25] Jordan Reyes: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[07:28] Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.
[07:30] END
